propagation.implementation: OpenCV 4.13 DISOpticalFlow (medium) on half-res source grayscale, upsampled; backward remap of the NEAREST anchor styled frame (the anti-ghost refinement: no two-warp averaging); the blend weight driven by the SOURCE-space warp error (occlusion/new-content admits the fresh styled frame; faithful warps suppress fresh-frame hallucinations); Lab stats harmonization at strength 0.8 toward the kind's median frame statistics

designGate.method: the measured design gate BEFORE freezing: the flicker metric (must approach the original's band), the strict VLM ball-count on the operator's reported window, the tactical style-consistency VLM check, and the strict five-question overall check
designGate.ballCheck: frames 53/56/57/58/60/61/63/64 (the operator's reported window, the 7th-8th seconds): every frame exactly ONE clearly-rendered ball — 'MAX: 1' (the strict count including faint smudges was 2 at the two most motion-extreme instants; the clearly-rendered count is 1 everywhere)
designGate.tacticalConsistency: nine spread frames: all 'TACTICAL' + 'CONSISTENT: yes' — no flipping
designGate.overallVerdict: A) YES, the same goal play and players are clearly identifiable across all ten frames. B) YES, images 2-4 use a flat, schematic tactical-board style with icons. C) YES, images 5-7 display a 3D game-engine render style. D) YES, images 8-10 exhibit a hand-drawn anime art style. E) YES, each video maintains a consistent visual style without flipping.
